issue_context.title: [KMSv2] Add support for hot reload of the `EncryptionConfiguration`
issue_context.body:
- Watch on the `EncryptionConfiguration`
- When changes are detected, process the `EncryptionConfiguration` resource, and add new transformers and update existing ones atomically.
- If there is an issue with creating or updating any of the transformers, retain the current configuration in the kube-apiserver and generate an error in logs.

ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-auth/3299-kms-v2-improvements

/sig auth

review_comments: document that this hash is only expected to be used in memory and this function has no cross-release stability guarantees
Store the result of these `filepath.Join`s in variables with meaningful names.  Otherwise it hard to tell what is being written / symlinked.
Oh I just thought of something - hot reloading will make us lose the DEK cache.  Hmm 🤔
Created https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/113497 for tracking.
`.Set` no longer needs to take `inFlight` as input.
This should track the timeout.
just to check, this is passing in a subcontext of the server stop context, which will close when either the server stopCh is closed or when we call closeTransformers(), right?
Correct.
We seem to be using both `path.Join` and `filepath.Join`.  Update this file to only use `filepath.Join`.
document the expected lifespan of this stop channel (I *think* it's the server lifetime)
yup. added a comment.
implemented.

there are edges around handling of paths containing symlinks we want to make sure we handle (since that's how a mounted-in configmap would surface). I *think* we have to watch parent dirs as well in case they are symlinks

Added tests to handle EC file updated by
- truncate (os.WriteFile)
- deleteAndCreate (os.Remove and then os.Create)
- move (write new config in another tmp dir then os.Rename to move it to dir being watched by watchers)
- symLink (created config in parentDir, created symLink of same in dir being watched by watchers, and then update parent dir.)
are we calling closeTransformers() consistently in the error cases below where we return?
just to verify, this is also a subcontext of the server stop channel?
correct.
document what the string return value is
Create an issue for this.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/113704

can be a follow-up, but add a TODO so that past this point we always increment or bump a timestamp metric indicating encryption config reload either with result=success or result=error, so an external observer can tell when their updated config is effective, and if we're looping unexpectedly here
added a note.
Any reason for having named return parameters just for this function? `configChanged` is really just used in the return statements and never set anywhere in code.
To give readability to the code. Returning simply bool is confusing as to what it is used for.
This var should be moved up since it can be used in both cases.
This function should not return until all of its control loops have exited (i.e. use a wait group to track the child go routines, probably via a defer)
This is arguably a nit and not necessarily a hard requirement.
I thought about it, but we are passing stop-ch from Run to the child go routines so there won't be any leak.
Oh I am not concerned about a leak here - I am saying that `.Run` is blocking, and when it returns, I would expect all of its child go routines to have stopped.  But this is good enough for now.

Add some assertions about `KMSTimeout` in this test (`TestEncryptionProviderConfigCorrect`) because we have a lot of untested math in `LoadEncryptionConfig` (plus we need to check that defaulting actually does what we expect).
I am testing most math in the `TestKMSMaxTimeout`.  But will also add some assertions in the `TestEncryptionProviderConfigCorrect` to test the `KMSCloseGracePeriod` as well.
This should take `maxTimeout` as input.
This should just `.Load` and check the single healthz that it requires.
shouldn't the `kms: always use single kms-provider-0 healthz endpoint` commit be dropped if this is based on the latest version of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/113529?
I think we still need the `complete` bool to make sure we call the `Complete()` method exactly once, don't we?
that's not part of that commit, is it? (I left this comment on the first line of that commit... I'm not suggesting the `complete` field be dropped)
